claim: The lateral line system enables fishes and aquatic-stage amphibians to detect local water movement via mechanosensory hair cells in neuromasts.
source_text: The lateral line system enables fishes and aquatic-stage amphibians to detect local water movement via mechanosensory hair cells in neuromasts
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge about the lateral line system, supported by citations in the manuscript (Bullock et al., 1983; Northcutt, 1997; Mogdans, 2021).

claim: Many species detect weak electric fields via electroreceptors (modified hair cells) in ampullary organs.
source_text: many species to detect weak electric fields via electroreceptors (modified hair cells) in ampullary organs
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Both neuromasts and ampullary organs develop from lateral line placodes.
source_text: Both neuromasts and ampullary organs develop from lateral line placodes
evidence_reasoning: This is established developmental biology knowledge supported by citations (Northcutt, 1997; Piotrowski and Baker, 2014; Baker, 2019).

claim: The ancestral lineages of zebrafish (teleosts) and Xenopus (frogs) independently lost electroreception.
source_text: This is because the ancestral lineages of zebrafish (teleosts) and Xenopus (frogs) independently lost electroreception.
evidence_reasoning: This is established evolutionary knowledge supported by citations (Bullock et al., 1983; Baker et al., 2013; Crampton, 2019).

claim: Bmp5 was identified as a promising candidate via differential RNA-seq in the Mississippi paddlefish (Polyodon spathula).
source_text: We identified Bmp5 as a promising candidate via differential RNA-seq in an electroreceptive ray-finned fish, the Mississippi paddlefish ( Polyodon spathula ; Modrell et al., 2017, eLife 6: e24197).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from a previous study (Modrell et al., 2017) that performed differential RNA-seq.

claim: Bmp5 and four other Bmp pathway genes are expressed in the developing lateral line of sterlet sturgeon (Acipenser ruthenus).
source_text: In an experimentally tractable relative, the sterlet sturgeon ( Acipenser ruthenus ), we found that Bmp5 and four other Bmp pathway genes are expressed in the developing lateral line
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data presented in the manuscript (Figures 1, 3, and supplements).

claim: Bmp signalling is active in the developing lateral line of sterlet sturgeon.
source_text: we found that Bmp5 and four other Bmp pathway genes are expressed in the developing lateral line, and that Bmp signalling is active
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data showing pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity (Figure 2).

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis targeting Bmp5 in G0-injected sterlet embryos resulted in fewer ampullary organs.
source_text: Furthermore, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis targeting Bmp5 in G0-injected sterlet embryos resulted in fewer ampullary organs.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from CRISPR/Cas9 experiments presented in Figures 4 and 5, including statistical analysis.

claim: When Bmp signalling was inhibited by DMH1 treatment shortly before the formation of ampullary organ primordia, supernumerary ampullary organs developed.
source_text: Conversely, when Bmp signalling was inhibited by DMH1 treatment shortly before the formation of ampullary organ primordia, supernumerary ampullary organs developed.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from DMH1 treatment experiments presented in Figures 6, 7, and 8, including statistical analysis.

claim: Bmp5 promotes ampullary organ development.
source_text: These data suggest that Bmp5 promotes ampullary organ development
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the CRISPR/Cas9 data showing that disrupting Bmp5 leads to fewer ampullary organs.

claim: Bmp signalling via another ligand(s) prevents overproduction of ampullary organs.
source_text: whereas Bmp signalling via another ligand(s) prevents their overproduction
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the DMH1 treatment data showing that blocking Bmp signalling leads to supernumerary ampullary organs.

claim: Bmp signalling has opposing roles during ampullary organ formation.
source_text: Taken together, this demonstrates opposing roles for Bmp signalling during ampullary organ formation.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the combination of CRISPR/Cas9 and DMH1 treatment data showing both promoting and inhibiting roles.

claim: Neuromasts detect local water movement via mechanosensory hair cells whose apical surfaces are embedded in a gelatinous cupula.
source_text: Neuromasts, arranged in characteristic lines across the head and trunk, detect local water movement via mechanosensory hair cells ('touch at a distance') whose apical surfaces are embedded in a gelatinous cupula
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about neuromast structure and function, supported by citations.

claim: In non-teleost electroreceptive fishes and amphibians, fields of electrosensory ampullary organs flank some or all of the neuromast lines on the head.
source_text: In non-teleost electroreceptive fishes and amphibians, fields of electrosensory ampullary organs flank some or all of the neuromast lines on the head
evidence_reasoning: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations (Bullock et al., 1983; Baker et al., 2013; Crampton, 2019).

claim: The electrosensory division of the lateral line system was independently lost in several lineages, including those leading to frogs/toads and to teleost fishes.
source_text: The electrosensory division of the lateral line system was independently lost in several lineages, for example, those leading to frogs/toads and to teleost fishes
evidence_reasoning: This is established evolutionary knowledge supported by citations (Bullock et al., 1983; Baker et al., 2013; Crampton, 2019).

claim: Electroreception with physiologically distinct electroreceptors independently evolved multiple times in a few groups of teleost fishes.
source_text: although electroreception with physiologically distinct electroreceptors independently evolved multiple times in a few groups of teleost fishes
evidence_reasoning: This is established evolutionary knowledge supported by citations (Bullock et al., 1983; Baker et al., 2013; Crampton, 2019).

claim: Non-teleost ampullary organs have a 'flask-shaped' chamber with a sensory epithelium at the base, connected to a pore in the epidermis via a canal filled with an electrically conductive jelly.
source_text: Non-teleost ampullary organs have a 'flask-shaped' chamber with a sensory epithelium at the base, connected to a pore in the epidermis via a canal filled with an electrically conductive jelly
evidence_reasoning: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations (Jørgensen, 2011; Josberger et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018).

claim: Ampullary electroreceptor cells are modified hair cells.
source_text: Ampullary electroreceptor cells are modified hair cells
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Jørgensen, 2005; Baker and Modrell, 2018; Baker, 2019).

claim: Ampullary electroreceptor cells respond to weak cathodal (exterior-negative) electric fields, primarily for detecting prey or avoiding predators.
source_text: that respond to weak cathodal (exterior-negative) electric fields, primarily for detecting prey or avoiding predators
evidence_reasoning: This is established functional knowledge supported by citations (Bodznick and Montgomery, 2005; Crampton, 2019; Leitch and Julius, 2019; Chagnaud et al., 2021).

claim: Both neuromasts and ampullary organs contain several types of support cells that flank the sensory receptor cells.
source_text: Both neuromasts and ampullary organs contain several types of support cells that flank the sensory receptor cells
evidence_reasoning: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations (Cernuda-Cernuda and García-Fernández, 1996; Camacho et al., 2007; Russell et al., 2022).

claim: In zebrafish neuromasts, both active and quiescent stem cell populations have been identified amongst the various support cell populations.
source_text: In zebrafish neuromasts, both active and quiescent stem cell populations have been identified amongst the various support cell populations
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from zebrafish studies, supported by citations (Lush and Piotrowski, 2014; Lush et al., 2019; Undurraga et al., 2019).

claim: Neuromasts, ampullary organs and their afferent neurons all develop from a series of lateral line placodes on the head.
source_text: Neuromasts, ampullary organs and their afferent neurons all develop from a series of lateral line placodes (thickened patches of neurogenic ectoderm) on the head
evidence_reasoning: This is established developmental knowledge supported by citations (Northcutt, 1997; Piotrowski and Baker, 2014; Baker, 2019).

claim: There are six bilateral pairs of lateral line placodes.
source_text: There are six bilateral pairs of lateral line placodes: the anterodorsal, anteroventral and otic lateral line placodes form rostral to the otic vesicle, whereas the middle, supratemporal and posterior lateral line placodes form caudal to the otic vesicle
evidence_reasoning: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations (Northcutt, 1997; Piotrowski and Baker, 2014; Baker, 2019).

claim: Neuroblasts delaminate from the pole of each placode lying closest to the otic vesicle and form afferent bipolar neurons.
source_text: Neuroblasts delaminate from the pole of each placode lying closest to the otic vesicle; they form afferent bipolar neurons (which coalesce in lateral line ganglia)
evidence_reasoning: This is established developmental knowledge supported by citations (Piotrowski and Baker, 2014; McGraw et al., 2017; Chitnis, 2021).

claim: The Mississippi paddlefish (Polyodon spathula) has more ampullary organs than any other species.
source_text: the Mississippi paddlefish (Polyodon spathula), which has more ampullary organs than any other species
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Chagnaud et al., 2021).

claim: A differential bulk RNA-seq screen comparing gene expression in fin tissue versus operculum tissue in paddlefish resulted in a lateral line-enriched gene-set containing almost 500 candidate genes enriched by at least twofold.
source_text: To identify candidate genes potentially involved in ampullary organ development, we performed a differential bulk RNA-seq screen at late-larval stages, comparing gene expression in fin tissue (which lacks lateral line organs) versus operculum tissue (which has many ampullary organs and some neuromasts). This resulted in a lateral line-enriched gene-set containing almost 500 candidate genes enriched by at least twofold in paddlefish opercular versus fin tissue
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from a previous study (Modrell et al., 2017a).

claim: Bmp5 was 2.5-fold enriched in late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue.
source_text: One gene present in the paddlefish lateral line-enriched gene set was the Bmp ligand gene Bmp5 (2.5-fold enriched in late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue; Modrell et al., 2017a).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from a previous study (Modrell et al., 2017a).

claim: At stage 37, faint Bmp5 expression was seen within developing gill filaments but there was no detectable lateral line expression in sterlet.
source_text: At stage 37, faint Bmp5 expression was seen within developing gill filaments but there was no detectable lateral line expression
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: By stage 40, strong Bmp5 expression was visible in mature neuromasts as well as ampullary organ primordia in sterlet.
source_text: By stage 40, strong Bmp5 expression was visible in mature neuromasts as well as ampullary organ primordia
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: At stage 42, Bmp5 expression was seen in mature ampullary organs but seemed weaker in neuromasts in sterlet.
source_text: At stage 42, Bmp5 expression was seen in mature ampullary organs but seemed weaker in neuromasts
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1I and J.

claim: By stage 45, Bmp5 expression persisted in ampullary organs and was no longer seen in most neuromasts on the head in sterlet.
source_text: By stage 45, Bmp5 expression persisted in ampullary organs, although this seemed weaker than at stage 40, and was no longer seen in most neuromasts on the head
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1M and N.

claim: Bmp5 is expressed early in developing ampullary organs and transiently in mature neuromasts.
source_text: Overall, these results suggest that Bmp5 is expressed early within ampullary organ primordia and maintained in mature ampullary organs at least through to the onset of independent feeding at stage 45. In contrast, Bmp5 only seems to be expressed in mature neuromasts, after the onset of hair cell differentiation, and then only transiently.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the time-course of Bmp5 expression data shown in Figure 1.

claim: At stage 30, faint pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in the region of the anteroventral lateral line primordium in sterlet.
source_text: At stage 30 (the earliest stage examined), faint pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in the region of the anteroventral lateral line primordium
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: By stage 34, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was detectable in lateral line primordia, with a ring pattern around developing neuromast primordia in sterlet.
source_text: By stage 34, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was detectable in lateral line primordia, with a ring pattern around developing neuromast primordia in the otic/anterodorsal and anteroventral primordia
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: At stage 36, weak pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen around developing neuromasts and more prominent immunoreactivity was seen in a filamentous pattern that likely corresponds to lateral line nerves in sterlet.
source_text: At stage 36, weak pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was still seen around developing neuromasts, but we were intrigued to see more prominent immunoreactivity in a filamentous pattern that seemed most likely to correspond to lateral line nerves
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2E and F, with inference about the identity of the filamentous pattern.

claim: At stage 40, diffuse pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in regions flanking the nerves where ampullary organ primordia are forming in sterlet.
source_text: At stage 40, diffuse immunoreactivity was also seen in regions flanking the nerves where ampullary organ primordia are forming
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2I and J.

claim: By stage 42, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was visible in ampullary organs and much less prominent in lateral line nerves in sterlet.
source_text: By stage 42, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was visible in ampullary organs and much less prominent in lateral line nerves
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2K and L.

claim: At stages 43 and 45, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was visible at the periphery rather than centre of neuromasts and ampullary organs in sterlet.
source_text: At stages 43 and 45, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was more clearly visible in neuromasts as well as ampullary organs, in all cases at the periphery rather than centre of each organ
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2M-P.

claim: The peripheral pattern of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity suggests that Bmp signalling is active in supporting cells rather than receptor cells.
source_text: This peripheral pattern of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity suggests that Bmp signalling is active in supporting cells rather than receptor cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the spatial pattern of immunoreactivity relative to known cell types in lateral line organs.

claim: Bmp signalling is active throughout lateral line development in the sterlet.
source_text: Overall, these data suggest that Bmp signalling is active throughout lateral line development in the sterlet, including lateral line organ primordia and even lateral line nerves, and later at the periphery (rather than the centre) of maturing ampullary organs and neuromasts, suggesting activity in supporting cells rather than receptor cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the comprehensive time-course of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Bmp4 was not expressed in the developing sterlet lateral line at stage 37 or stage 38.
source_text: Bmp4 expression was not evident in the developing sterlet lateral line at stage 37 or stage 38
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: By stage 40, diffuse Bmp4 expression was observed in neuromast regions and fields of ampullary organ primordia on the head in sterlet.
source_text: By stage 40, diffuse Bmp4 expression was observed in neuromast regions and fields of ampullary organ primordia on the head
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: At stage 42, Bmp4 expression in lateral line regions on the head was almost gone in sterlet.
source_text: At stage 42, Bmp4 expression in lateral line regions on the head was almost gone, with only faint expression remaining in the dorsal infraorbital ampullary organ field, just below the eye
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3H and I.

claim: By stage 45, Bmp4 was no longer expressed in lateral line regions on the head in sterlet.
source_text: By stage 45, Bmp4 was no longer expressed in lateral line regions on the head
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3K-L.

claim: Bmp4 plays a more transient role than Bmp5 in lateral line organ development.
source_text: These data suggest that Bmp4 plays a more transient role than Bmp5 in lateral line organ development.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from comparing the time-courses of Bmp4 and Bmp5 expression data.

claim: An as-yet unidentified Bmp ligand gene is expressed in lateral line primordia before either Bmp5 or Bmp4.
source_text: Furthermore, most likely an as-yet unidentified Bmp ligand gene is expressed in lateral line primordia before either Bmp5 or Bmp4, given that pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was detectable in lateral line primordia at stage 34
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the presence of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity at stage 34 before Bmp5 or Bmp4 expression is detected.

claim: Sostdc1 was 4.2-fold enriched in late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue.
source_text: Sostdc1 (sclerostin domain-containing 1; also known as Wise, Ectodin) is a secreted antagonist of both the Bmp and Wnt pathways (Tong et al., 2022). Sostdc1 was 4.2-fold enriched in late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from a previous study (Modrell et al., 2017a).

claim: From stage 36 onwards, Sostdc1 expression was seen in lines of differentiated neuromasts in sterlet.
source_text: From stage 36 onwards, Sostdc1 expression was seen in lines of differentiated neuromasts (and in gill filament primordia) on the head
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-M.

claim: At stage 42, Sostdc1 expression was detected in ampullary organs in sterlet.
source_text: At stage 42, Sostdc1 expression was also detected in ampullary organs
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2H and I.

claim: Sostdc1 plays a persistent role within neuromasts, but any function in ampullary organ development is likely to be transient.
source_text: These data suggest Sostdc1 plays a persistent role within neuromasts, but any function in ampullary organ development is likely to be transient.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the time-course of Sostdc1 expression data.

claim: Apcdd1 was 2.2-fold enriched in late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue.
source_text: Apcdd1 (adenomatosis polyposis coli down-regulated 1) is also a secreted inhibitor of both the Bmp and Wnt pathways (Vonica et al., 2020). Apcdd1 was 2.2-fold enriched in late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from a previous study (Modrell et al., 2017a).

claim: By stage 40, Apcdd1 expression was visible around ampullary organ primordia and some neuromasts on the head in sterlet.
source_text: By stage 40, expression was visible around ampullary organ primordia and some neuromasts on the head
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E and F.

claim: Apcdd1 may be more important for ampullary organ development than neuromast development.
source_text: These data, especially the early, broad expression within ampullary organ fields and seemingly very late upregulation in neuromasts, suggest that Apcdd1 may be more important for ampullary organ development.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the spatial and temporal pattern of Apcdd1 expression data.

claim: Both Bmp5 ohnologs have been retained in sterlet, on chromosomes 5 and 6, with 88.87% nucleotide identity in the coding sequence.
source_text: Searching the reference genome (Vertebrate Genomes Project NCBI RefSeq assembly GCF_902713425.1) for Bmp5 showed that both Bmp5 ohnologs have been retained, on chromosomes 5 and 6, with 88.87% nucleotide identity in the coding sequence (and 95.60% amino acid identity).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by analysis of the published sterlet genome sequence.

claim: All Bmp5 sgRNAs fully match the ohnolog on chromosome 6.
source_text: All of our Bmp5 sgRNAs fully match the ohnolog on chromosome 6.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by sequence analysis of the sgRNAs against the sterlet genome.

claim: sgRNAs 2 and 4 each have a single-base mismatch with the chromosome 5 ohnolog that should be tolerated.
source_text: Relative to the ohnolog on chromosome 5, sgRNAs 2 and 4 (Table 1; Figure 4A) each have a single-base mismatch, respectively, in positions 7 and 4 of the target sequence (PAM-distal), which should be tolerated
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by sequence analysis and established knowledge about sgRNA tolerance to mismatches (Guo et al., 2014; Rabinowitz and Offen, 2021).

claim: Relative to Tyr crispants, a mosaic reduction in Cacna1d expression in ampullary organ fields was observed in 46% of Bmp5 crispants.
source_text: relative to Tyr crispants (n=0/24; Figure 4A and B; Supplementary file 1), we observed a mosaic reduction in Cacna1d expression in ampullary organ fields in 46% of Bmp5 crispants (n=53/116; Figure 4C–F; Supplementary file 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from CRISPR/Cas9 experiments shown in Figure 4 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Of 43 genotyped Bmp5 crispants, 33 had a positive 'knock-out' score, confirming successful disruption of the targeted gene.
source_text: Of the 43 genotyped crispants, 33 had a positive 'knock-out' score, confirming successful disruption of the targeted gene
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by ICE analysis data shown in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Disrupting the Bmp5 gene prevented ampullary organ formation, rather than blocking the later differentiation of Kcnab3-positive electroreceptors within ampullary organs.
source_text: Furthermore, very few 'additional' ampullary organs appeared after Sox2 immunostaining (Figure 4J1,K1 and L1; compare with Figure 4J, K and L), suggesting that disrupting the Bmp5 gene prevented ampullary organ formation, rather than blocking the later differentiation of Kcnab3-positive electroreceptors within ampullary organs.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from comparing Kcnab3 expression with Sox2 immunostaining in the same crispants.

claim: Bmp5 crispants had significantly fewer ampullary organs overall than Tyr control crispants (p<0.0001).
source_text: Statistical analysis using a two-tailed Mann-Whitney (Wilcoxon rank sum) test revealed that Bmp5 crispants had significantly fewer ampullary organs overall than Tyr control crispants (p<0.0001; Figure 5A).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis of ampullary organ counts shown in Figure 5A and Supplementary file 2.

claim: All ampullary organ fields except for the dorsal supraorbital field had significantly fewer ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants versus control Tyr crispants.
source_text: Indeed, all ampullary organ fields except for the dorsal supraorbital field (one of the smaller fields) had significantly fewer ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants versus control Tyr crispants
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis of ampullary organ counts in individual fields shown in Figure 5B and Supplementary file 2.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeting of Bmp5 in G0-injected embryos led to significantly fewer ampullary organs developing in almost all fields.
source_text: Overall, these data show that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeting of Bmp5 in G0-injected embryos led to significantly fewer ampullary organs developing in almost all fields.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the comprehensive CRISPR/Cas9 experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Bmp5 normally acts to promote ampullary organ formation.
source_text: This suggests that Bmp5, which is expressed in ampullary organ primordia as well as in mature ampullary organs (Figure 1), normally acts to promote ampullary organ formation.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the CRISPR/Cas9 data showing that disrupting Bmp5 leads to fewer ampullary organs.

claim: More ampullary organs had formed by stage 45 in all DMH1-treated larvae compared to DMSO controls.
source_text: In comparison to DMSO controls (n=12), more ampullary organs had formed by stage 45 in all DMH1-treated larvae (n=17/17), as visualised by ISH for the hair cell/electroreceptor marker Cacna1d (Figure 6A–D; n=8) or for electroreceptor-specific Kcnab3 (Figure 6E–H; n=9).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from DMH1 treatment experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: The increase in ampullary organ number after DMH1 treatment was most striking in the dorsalmost ampullary organ fields.
source_text: The increase in ampullary organ number seemed to be general but was most striking in the dorsalmost ampullary organ fields, i.e., the dorsal supraorbital, dorsal otic and supratemporal fields.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from DMH1 treatment experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: The supernumerary ampullary organs in the dorsal region of DMH1-treated larvae at stage 45 were ectopic, rather than precocious.
source_text: ISH for Cacna1d showed that the three dorsal ampullary organ fields were still clearly separate even in much older larvae (Figure 6I and J), suggesting that the supernumerary ampullary organs in this region of DMH1-treated larvae at stage 45 were ectopic, rather than precocious.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from comparing DMH1-treated larvae with older wild-type larvae.

claim: Ectopic offshoots of the supraorbital neuromast line were seen in a majority of larvae (71%) in which Bmp signalling had been blocked for 20 hr from stage 36.
source_text: Overall, therefore, ectopic offshoots of the supraorbital neuromast line (compare Figure 6M1,N1 with wildtype Sox2 expression at stage 45 in Figure 2—figure supplement 1K and L) were seen in a majority of larvae (n=10/14; 71%) in which Bmp signalling had been blocked for 20 hr from stage 36
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from DMH1 treatment experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: DMH1-treated larvae had significantly more ampullary organs overall than DMSO controls (p<0.0001).
source_text: Statistical analysis using a two-tailed Mann-Whitney (Wilcoxon rank sum) test confirmed that DMH1-treated larvae had significantly more ampullary organs overall than DMSO controls (p<0.0001; Figure 7A).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis of ampullary organ counts shown in Figure 7A and Supplementary file 3.

claim: All individual ampullary organ fields had significantly more ampullary organs in DMH1-treated larvae than in DMSO controls.
source_text: This was also the case for each individual ampullary organ field (Figure 7B; Supplementary file 3).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis of ampullary organ counts in individual fields shown in Figure 7B and Supplementary file 3.

claim: DMH1-treated larvae had significantly more ampullary organs than older (2.0/2.8 cm) wild-type larvae, both overall (p<0.0001) and in all fields except the ventral supraorbital and posterior preopercular fields.
source_text: Furthermore, the DMH1-treated larvae (n=17) had significantly more ampullary organs than older (2.0/2.8 cm) wild-type larvae (n=10), both overall (p<0.0001; Figure 8A) and in all fields except the ventral supraorbital and posterior preopercular fields
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis of ampullary organ counts shown in Figure 8 and Supplementary file 3.

claim: Blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36 results in supernumerary ampullary organs in all fields.
source_text: Overall, these results show that blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36, before the first ampullary organ primordia form, results in supernumerary ampullary organs in all fields.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the comprehensive DMH1 treatment experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claim: During normal development, Bmp signalling dampens ampullary organ formation, preventing the over-production of ampullary organs in each individual field and the formation of ectopic ampullary organs in the most dorsal fields.
source_text: This suggests that during normal development, Bmp signalling dampens ampullary organ formation, preventing the over-production of ampullary organs in each individual field and the formation of ectopic ampullary organs in the most dorsal fields.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the DMH1 treatment data showing that blocking Bmp signalling leads to supernumerary and ectopic ampullary organs.

claim: During normal development, Bmp5 promotes ampullary organ formation.
source_text: We began by investigating Bmp5, the only Bmp ligand gene in our late-larval paddlefish lateral line organ-enriched gene-set (Modrell et al., 2017a). In sterlet, Bmp5 proved to be expressed in ampullary organ primordia (though not neuromast primordia), as well as in mature ampullary organs and neuromasts. Significantly fewer ampullary organs formed when Bmp5 was targeted for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis in G0-injected sterlet embryos, suggesting that during normal development, Bmp5 promotes ampullary organ formation.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the CRISPR/Cas9 data showing that disrupting Bmp5 leads to fewer ampullary organs.

claim: Bmp signalling activity is required to prevent too many ampullary organs from developing.
source_text: In contrast, blocking Bmp signalling globally at stages just prior to the onset of ampullary organ development led to significantly more ampullary organs forming in all fields. Hence, Bmp signalling activity is required to prevent too many ampullary organs from developing.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the DMH1 treatment data showing that blocking Bmp signalling leads to supernumerary ampullary organs.

claim: Bmp4 is an early marker for all sensory patches in the chicken inner ear, and for the cristae in mouse.
source_text: Bmp4 is an early marker for all sensory patches in the chicken inner ear, and for the cristae (vestibular sensory patches of the semicircular canals) in mouse
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from inner ear development studies, supported by citations (Wu and Oh, 1996; Morsli et al., 1998).

claim: Bmp4 is required for the formation of the cristae in mouse.
source_text: Conditional knockout experiments showed that Bmp4 is required for the formation of the cristae
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from conditional knockout studies, supported by citation (Chang et al., 2008).

claim: Bmp signalling is required for the induction of the cochlear-duct prosensory domain that forms the organ of Corti.
source_text: conditional knockout of the type I receptor genes Bmpr1a (Alk3) and Bmpr1b (Alk6) showed that Bmp signalling is also required for the induction of the cochlear-duct prosensory domain that forms the organ of Corti
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from conditional knockout studies, supported by citation (Ohyama et al., 2010).

claim: Intermediate levels of Bmp4 promote hair cell formation in cultured mouse otocysts.
source_text: Treatment of cultured mouse otocysts with different concentrations of Bmp4 revealed that intermediate levels of Bmp4 promote hair cell formation
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from in vitro studies, supported by citation (Ohyama et al., 2010).

claim: In the mature chicken auditory epithelium, Bmp4 secreted from existing hair cells prevents supporting cells from forming supernumerary hair cells.
source_text: Taken together, these results suggest that in the mature auditory epithelium, Bmp4 secreted from existing hair cells prevents supporting cells from forming supernumerary hair cells
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from chicken auditory epithelium studies, supported by citation (Lewis et al., 2018).

claim: After hair-cell death in chicken auditory epithelium, Bmp4 is lost and inhibition is relieved, allowing hair cell regeneration.
source_text: after hair-cell death, Bmp4 is lost and this inhibition is relieved, allowing hair cell regeneration
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from chicken auditory epithelium studies, supported by citation (Lewis et al., 2018).

claim: Foxg1 is expressed in paddlefish and sterlet in the central region of sensory ridges where neuromasts form.
source_text: We recently reported that the transcription factor gene Foxg1 is expressed in paddlefish and sterlet in the central region of sensory ridges where neuromasts form
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from a recent study (Minařík et al., 2024a).

claim: Targeting Foxg1 for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis led to ampullary organs forming within neuromast lines.
source_text: that targeting Foxg1 for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis led to ampullary organs forming within neuromast lines
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from a recent preprint (Minařík et al., 2024b).

claim: Lateral line primordia are 'poised' to form ampullary organs in electroreceptive species.
source_text: Taken together, this suggests that lateral line primordia are 'poised' to form ampullary organs (indeed potentially that ampullary organs are the 'default' fate for lateral line primordia in electroreceptive species; preprint, Minařík et al., 2024b)
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation based on the combined data from Foxg1 and Bmp signalling studies.

claim: Afferent innervation is not required for the formation of neuromasts deposited by lateral line primordia in zebrafish.
source_text: Afferent innervation is not required for the formation of neuromasts deposited by lateral line primordia in zebrafish
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from zebrafish studies, supported by citations (Andermann et al., 2002; Grant et al., 2005; López-Schier and Hudspeth, 2005).

claim: The post-embryonic budding of neuromasts to form short rows depends on Wnt signalling from afferent axons in zebrafish.
source_text: However, the post-embryonic budding of neuromasts to form short rows ('stitches') of additional neuromasts depends on Wnt signalling from afferent axons: this promotes cell proliferation within the neuromast, which is required for the budding process
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from zebrafish studies, supported by citations (Wada et al., 2013; Wada and Kawakami, 2015).

claim: Bmp signalling in the lateral line nerve may act to inhibit precocious budding of primary neuromasts during embryogenesis.
source_text: We speculate that Bmp signalling in the lateral line nerve may act to inhibit this process during embryogenesis, thus preventing precocious budding of primary neuromasts.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the pattern of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity in nerves and the ectopic neuromast phenotype after DMH1 treatment.

claim: The sterlet genome has retained a high level of tetraploidy, including around 70% of ohnologs.
source_text: Analysis of this genome showed that, rather than being functionally diploid as previously thought (from microsatellite data; Ludwig et al., 2001), the sterlet genome has retained a high level of tetraploidy, including around 70% of ohnologs (i.e., gene paralogs resulting from the independent whole-genome duplication in the sterlet lineage)
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from genome analysis, supported by citation (Du et al., 2020).

claim: Both Bmp5 ohnologs have 95.60% amino acid identity.
source_text: both Bmp5 ohnologs have been retained, on chromosomes 5 and 6, with 88.87% nucleotide identity in the coding sequence (and 95.60% amino acid identity)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by sequence analysis of the sterlet genome.

claim: The efficacy of different sgRNA combinations varied significantly in targeting Bmp5.
source_text: The efficacy of different sgRNA combinations varied significantly: injecting sgRNAs 2,3 led to fewer ampullary organs in 78% of cases (n=28/36; Supplementary file 1) versus 39% for sgRNAs 1,2,3 (n=16/41) and 23% for sgRNAs 1,4 (n=9/39; Supplementary file 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from CRISPR/Cas9 experiments shown in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Bmp5 is expressed in neuromast hair cell progenitor populations and downregulated as hair cells differentiate in zebrafish.
source_text: In mature neuromasts in zebrafish (at 5 dpf), scRNA-seq data show that Bmp5 is expressed in neuromast hair cell progenitor populations and downregulated as hair cells differentiate
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from scRNA-seq studies in zebrafish, supported by citation (Lush et al., 2019).

claim: Bmp5 is among the genes upregulated in 5-dpf zebrafish neuromasts within one hour after neomycin-induced hair cell death.
source_text: Furthermore, Bmp5 is among the genes upregulated in 5-dpf zebrafish neuromasts within one hour after neomycin-induced hair cell death
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from zebrafish regeneration studies, supported by citations (Jiang et al., 2014; Heller et al., 2022).

claim: Bmp5 may be important for hair cell regeneration.
source_text: Hence, Bmp5 may be important for hair cell regeneration.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the upregulation of Bmp5 after hair cell death in zebrafish and mouse.

claim: Neomycin treatment at late-larval stages in Siberian sturgeon kills electroreceptors as well as hair cells, both of which subsequently regenerate.
source_text: Neomycin treatment at late-larval stages (stages 44/45) in the Siberian sturgeon (A. baerii) kills electroreceptors, as well as hair cells, both of which subsequently regenerate
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from Siberian sturgeon studies, supported by citations (Fan et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2020).

claim: Bmp5 could play a role in the homeostasis and regeneration of electroreceptors as well as hair cells.
source_text: Given the expression of Bmp5 in mature ampullary organs and neuromasts in sterlet, Bmp5 could play a role in the homeostasis (and regeneration after injury) of electroreceptors as well as hair cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative hypothesis based on Bmp5 expression data in sterlet and regeneration data from other species.
